coracobrachialis muscle: Runs from the coracoid process to the middle of the medial surface of the humerus; the musculocutaneous nerve pierces it.
coracohumeral ligament: Runs from the coracoid process to the greater and lesser tubercles; it reinforces the rotator interval and thickens in frozen shoulder.
coracoid process: Beak-like process of the scapula projecting forwards; pectoralis minor, coracobrachialis and the short head of biceps attach to it.
corniculate cartilage: Small elastic cartilages sitting on the apex of the arytenoids; they support the aryepiglottic fold.
coronoid fossa: Anterior fossa above the trochlea; the coronoid process of the ulna enters it when the elbow is flexed.
coronoid process of ulna: Anterior projection of the trochlear notch; brachialis attaches to it and it can fracture in elbow dislocation.
corrugator supercilii: Draws the eyebrows medially and downwards, producing vertical wrinkles between them (frowning).
costal cartilage of eighth rib: False rib cartilage; it joins the cartilage above to form the costal arch.
costal cartilage of fifth rib: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.
costal cartilage of first rib: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.
costal cartilage of fourth rib: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.
costal cartilage of ninth rib: False rib cartilage; it joins the cartilage above to form the costal arch.
costal cartilage of second rib: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.
costal cartilage of seventh rib: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.
costal cartilage of sixth rib: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.
costal cartilage of tenth rib: False rib cartilage; it joins the cartilage above to form the costal arch.
costal cartilage of third rib: Hyaline cartilage joining the front end of the rib to the sternum or to the cartilage above; it gives the thoracic cage its flexibility.
costal groove: Groove on the inner surface of the lower border of the rib; the intercostal vein, artery and nerve run in it.
costal notches: Notches on the borders of the sternum; the costal cartilages articulate with the sternum here.
costal part of transverse process: Part of a lumbar transverse process that is a remnant of a rib.
costoclavicular ligament: Strong ligament binding the 1st costal cartilage to the lower surface of the clavicle; the most important stabiliser of the clavicle.
costotransverse ligament: Ligament binding the neck of the rib to the transverse process.
crest of greater tubercle: Ridge descending from the greater tubercle; pectoralis major attaches to it.
crest of head of rib: Ridge separating the two articular facets of the rib head; the intra-articular ligament attaches to it.
crest of lesser tubercle: Ridge descending from the lesser tubercle; teres major attaches to it.
crest of neck of rib: Upper border of the neck of the rib; the superior costotransverse ligament attaches to it.
cricoid cartilage: The only complete cartilaginous ring around the airway (at C6); narrow in front and broad behind. The trachea begins below it.
cricopharyngeal ligament: Ligament running from the apex of the arytenoid cartilages to the pharyngeal mucosa.
crown of tooth: Part of the tooth covered by enamel and visible in the mouth.
cruciform eminence: Cross-shaped elevation on the inner surface; the grooves of the dural sinuses meet here.
cruciform part of fibrous sheath of digi: Cruciform part of digital fibrous sheath
Crossed bands holding the flexor tendon sheath over the joints (C pulleys); with the A pulleys they stop the tendon bowstringing away from the bone.
crural fascia: Deep fascia enclosing the leg; by forming the muscle compartments it is the anatomical basis of compartment syndrome.
cuboid bone: Tarsal bone of the lateral column; the fibularis longus tendon runs in the groove on its lower surface.
cuneocuboid interosseous ligament: Interosseous ligament between the lateral cuneiform and the cuboid.
cuneometatarsal interosseous ligaments: Include the Lisfranc ligament from the medial cuneiform to the 2nd metatarsal; its injury leads to a Lisfranc fracture-dislocation.
cusp of tooth: Cusps on the chewing surface of the premolars and molars.
deep head of flexor pollicis brevis: Deep head of flexor pollicis brevis
Arises from the trapezoid and capitate; usually supplied by the ulnar nerve.
deep head of pronator teres: Small head arising from the coronoid process; the muscle pronates the forearm. Median nerve.
deep infrapatellar bursa: Between the patellar ligament and the tibia.
deep part of anterior compartment of for: Deep layer of anterior forearm compartment
deep part of masseter: Deep, vertical fibres of masseter; close and retract the jaw.
deep part of posterior compartment of fo: Deep layer of posterior forearm compartment
deep part of posterior compartment of le: Deep layer of posterior leg compartment
deep part of tibial collateral ligament: Deep part of medial collateral ligament
Deep fibres of the medial collateral ligament attached to the capsule and medial meniscus.
deep transverse metacarpal ligament: Ligament binding the heads of the 2nd–5th metacarpals together; the lumbricals pass in front of it and the interossei behind.
deep transverse metatarsal ligament: Ligament binding the five metatarsal heads together; the interdigital nerves can be compressed beneath it (Morton's neuroma).
deltoid muscle: Triangular muscle covering the shoulder; its clavicular, acromial and spinal parts insert into the deltoid tuberosity of the humerus. Axillary nerve (C5–C6); it can be paralysed in fractures of the surgical neck.
deltoid tubercle: Prominence on the spine of the scapula; deltoid and trapezius attach to it.
deltoid tuberosity: Rough area on the lateral surface of the humeral shaft; deltoid inserts here.
dens axis: Tooth-like process projecting up from the axis; the atlas rotates around it, producing the 'no' movement of the head.
